places.name: Chiostro del Bramante
places.note: Bramante's first Roman work, a cloister of perfect proportion two streets from Piazza Navona. The upstairs café looks into Raphael's Sibyls next door.

places.name: Tempietto del Bramante
places.address: Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio 2
places.note: A small round temple in a courtyard on the Gianicolo, the High Renaissance distilled to a single room. Walk up from Trastevere and stay for the view.

places.name: Quartiere Coppedè
places.note: A few streets of fantasy built between 1913 and 1927: Art Nouveau, Gothic and Baroque at once, with a frog fountain in the middle. Come on a Sunday morning.

places.name: Centrale Montemartini
places.note: Classical marbles set among the turbines of a 1912 power station. Goddesses against cast iron. One of the city's least crowded museums.

places.name: Giardino degli Aranci
places.note: An orange grove on the Aventine with the whole city spread out below. Afterwards, look through the keyhole at the Knights of Malta gate down the road.

places.name: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj
places.note: A private family palace that still lives on the Corso. Velázquez's Innocent X hangs in its own small room. Take the audio guide narrated by a prince of the family.

places.name: MAXXI
places.note: Zaha Hadid's concrete ribbons, stairs that fly through the void. Come for the building as much as the art, and walk the piazza after dark.

places.name: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana
places.note: The 'square Colosseum': arches stacked six by nine in white travertine. Rationalist, unsettling, beautiful. Now Fendi's headquarters; the ground floor hosts exhibitions.

places.name: Roscioli Salumeria
places.note: A delicatessen with tables among the hams and cheeses. Carbonara as a reference point, and a wine list to match. Book; then get bread from their bakery round the corner.

places.name: Bar San Calisto
places.note: An unrenovated bar where Trastevere still drinks. Plastic chairs, cheap Peroni, a famous chocolate. The antidote to the aperitivo terraces.

places.name: Drink Kong
places.address: Piazza di San Martino ai Monti 8
places.note: A neon-lit cocktail bar in Monti, all Blade Runner red. Inventive drinks, serious hospitality. Arrive early or expect to wait.

places.name: Pantheon
places.note: The dome with an open eye, still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world. Come when it rains.

places.name: Villa Farnesina
places.note: A banker's Renaissance villa with Raphael's Galatea and painted loggias. Quiet, even at the height of summer.

places.name: Palazzo Altemps
places.note: Classical sculpture displayed in a calm Renaissance palace, among them the Ludovisi Throne. A short walk from Navona and far quieter.

places.name: Galleria Borghese
places.note: Bernini's marble made to look like flesh, in a cardinal's villa. Timed entry only; book weeks ahead.

places.name: Villa Giulia
places.note: A papal villa with a sunken nymphaeum, holding the Etruscan collection. Don't miss the Sarcophagus of the Spouses.

places.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
places.note: Borromini's star-plan church with a spiralling lantern. Usually open only on Sunday mornings.

places.name: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane
places.note: Borromini's tiny oval church; the dome's coffering shrinks as it rises. Small enough to fit inside one of St Peter's piers.

places.name: Basilica di San Clemente
places.note: Three churches stacked through time: a medieval basilica over an early church over a Mithraic temple. Listen for running water below.

places.name: Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta
places.note: Piranesi's only built work, a square of obelisks and trophies. Look through the keyhole at the dome of St Peter's.

places.name: Non-Catholic Cemetery
places.note: Keats and Shelley lie under cypresses beside a marble pyramid. Cats sleep on the graves.

places.name: Villa Doria Pamphilj
places.note: Rome's largest park: umbrella pines, formal gardens and a casino on the hill. Where the city goes to run.

places.name: Mercato di Testaccio
places.note: A modern covered market above Roman ruins, with stalls for supplì and sandwiches. Lunch at the counters.

places.name: Ara Pacis
places.note: Augustus's altar of peace in Richard Meier's glass box by the Tiber. Ancient relief carving in full daylight.

places.name: Palazzetto dello Sport
places.note: Nervi's 1957 concrete dome resting on Y-shaped buttresses. A lesson in structure from the street.

places.name: Auditorium Parco della Musica
places.note: Renzo Piano's three halls like giant lute bodies around an open-air cavea. Catch a concert or simply walk around.

places.name: Keats-Shelley House
places.note: The room where Keats died, at the foot of the Spanish Steps, now a library for the Romantic poets. Look down on the steps from the window.

places.name: Sant'Eustachio Il Caffè
places.note: Espresso since 1938, roasted over wood and served already sweetened, with a thick crema. Drink it standing at the bar.

places.name: Armando al Pantheon
places.note: A family trattoria a few steps from the Pantheon since 1961. Roman classics done properly; book.

places.name: Gelateria del Teatro
places.note: Gelato made in sight of the street, with flavours like sage and raspberry. On the prettiest street in the centre.

places.name: Biblioteca Angelica
places.note: One of Europe's first public libraries, a vaulted hall lined with wooden shelves and ladders. Ask at the desk to see the reading room.

places.name: Hotel Locarno Bar
places.note: A 1920s hotel bar with a garden terrace near Piazza del Popolo. Negroni, low lamps, old Rome.
